scope: REPORTING-AND-ROUTING-ONLY — this suite cannot cover parallel dispatch. A subagent cannot spawn subagents, so `Task` does not exist in any executor this repo runs, and `reviewer-*` are never actually dispatched here. What is graded is which reviewers the run DREW for a given diff (the .dispatch-log artifact) and whether the report SAYS the specialists did not run. Real dispatch has one arm only, and it is manual: see README.md 'The top-level arm (Option A)'.
notes: Executor harness + grading: see README.md 'Skill evals'. Each eval instantiates a fixture into a temp workdir with its own setup — which seeds a git repo and then applies one pending change, so the diff to review is the uncommitted working-tree change — and a fresh-context subagent executes skills/review/SKILL.md as /flywheel:review in that dir. Brief the executor: the host Task tool is unavailable, so reviewer dispatch goes through ./dispatch-reviewer <reviewer-name>, which records the request and returns no findings — whatever lens it draws it must review itself, in this one context; and the synthesized review is saved to review.md in the workdir root. Point it at skills/review/SKILL.md and nothing else under this repo — in particular not evals/. Grade with: bash skills/review/evals/check.sh <id> <workdir>.

evals.name: docs-only-draws-correctness-alone
evals.setup: cp -r skills/review/evals/fixtures/docs-change-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q -b main && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A -- . ':!pending' && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed && git -C "$W" apply pending/docs.patch && rm -rf "$W/pending"
evals.expected_output: The diff is 37 added lines of prose and two code comments, with no executable change anywhere. The routing rule is unambiguous — correctness alone — and the report names the reviewers it skipped and why.
expectations: .dispatch-log records no security reviewer — nothing in the diff touches input handling, auth, secrets or dependencies
.dispatch-log records no performance reviewer — nothing in the diff touches loops, queries, I/O or data volume
The report names both lenses it skipped (a silent cap reads as full coverage)

evals.name: input-handling-draws-security
evals.setup: cp -r skills/review/evals/fixtures/ops-console-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q -b main && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A -- . ':!pending' && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed && git -C "$W" apply pending/security.patch && rm -rf "$W/pending"
evals.expected_output: 65 added lines wiring the `filter` query parameter straight after WHERE over a database that also holds the console's own api_tokens, plus a hardcoded fallback token compared with ==. The security rule fires, and the review finds the defect rather than only routing correctly.
expectations: .dispatch-log records a security reviewer — the diff touches input handling, secrets and auth
.dispatch-log records reviewer-correctness, which is drawn for every diff
The report cites the changed file and names the class of problem (injection / interpolation / unparameterized SQL / a hardcoded credential)
The report says the specialists did not actually run (Option B), rather than reading as if a fan-out happened

evals.name: cross-domain-draws-the-full-fan-out
evals.setup: cp -r skills/review/evals/fixtures/ops-console-repo "$W" && git -C "$W" init -q -b main && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e add -A -- . ':!pending' && git -C "$W" -c user.email=e@e -c user.name=e commit -qm seed && git -C "$W" apply pending/fanout.patch && rm -rf "$W/pending"
evals.expected_output: 43 added lines crossing all three domains at once: a collector URL taken from a query parameter (input handling), a new pinned dependency (dependencies), one query and one HTTP POST per row inside a loop (loops, queries, I/O). The full three-way dispatch is routed — and this is the case where a report is most tempted to read as if three specialists reviewed in parallel.
expectations: .dispatch-log records all three reviewers — correctness, security and performance
The report says the specialists did not actually run (Option B), rather than reading as if a fan-out happened
